commentary: Twenty-nine years in freight and the basics still win: answer the phone, pay your carriers on time, and never promise a lane you cannot cover. Proud of the team at WFS.
Fall cohort of the TN Freight Mentorship Program is filling up. If you are new to brokering in Tennessee and want a mentor, reach out to me or Keith Burgess. We learn by doing.
Whitaker Freight Services is refreshing carrier vetting for all automotive parts clients this quarter. Safety scores, authority, and insurance checked top to bottom. Shippers, ask us how we vet.
Reminder to every broker and carrier I work with: keep your FMCSA authority and insurance current. A lapsed cert can shut down a load fast. We check before every booking.
Honored to co-lead the TN Freight Mentorship Program with Floyd Whitaker again this year. The freight business needs good people who do it the right way. Applications open now.
Our next quarterly DOT compliance webinar is scheduled for October 23. Open to TN Freight Association members. We will cover the latest FMCSA updates and carrier vetting best practices.
Welcoming my son Brandon to Whitaker Freight Services as a junior associate. He is learning carrier sales and dispatch the hard way, same as I did. Glad to have him on the team.
Save the date: the Tennessee Freight Association annual conference is October 10 at the Volunteer Conference Center in Knoxville. Registration and the agenda will post soon.
Ag season ramps up and capacity tightens every year. If you move grain or building materials in the Southeast, lock your lanes early. Late booking costs you more than the freight.
We are evaluating new freight software at WFS. Looking hard at RoutePoint Logistics Suite. If you run a small brokerage on a modern TMS, I would value your honest take. Comment or DM me.
Thank you to Floyd Whitaker and the WFS team for serving on the TN Freight Association board this year. Your work on the mentorship program is making a real difference for newcomers.
Eighteen years running Whitaker Freight Services this month. Started with a phone, a laptop, and a list of carriers I trusted. Thankful for the clients and carriers who grew with us.
Good carriers are the backbone of this business. Shout out to Ridgeline Trucking, Cumberland Gap Carriers, and Volunteer Logistics for covering tough automotive lanes this spring.
Freight brokering is a relationship business dressed up as a transaction. The rate gets the call, but service keeps the account. Twenty-nine years says that has not changed.
Three months into the TN Freight Mentorship Program and I have learned more from Floyd Whitaker about carrier vetting than a year on my own. Grateful for brokers who give back.
Headed to the TN Freight Association conference October 10 in Knoxville. If you are a broker or carrier in the Southeast, come find me. Always glad to talk lanes and meet new folks.
Now hiring a freight broker in Knoxville. Automotive and ag experience a plus, but we will train the right person who shows up and works hard. Apply through our page.
Spent the morning vetting carriers for our automotive parts clients. Authority active, insurance current, safety scores clean. Boring work that keeps freight moving and shippers happy.
Cumberland Auto Parts has trusted Whitaker Freight Services with our Southeast lanes for years. When you need a broker who actually answers the phone, Floyd is your guy.
Fuel prices, capacity swings, and tighter margins. The freight market is never boring. Best advice I give new brokers: build cash reserves and never stop vetting your carriers.
Big weekend ahead: over-40 softball Saturday morning, then smoking a brisket for the family. Even a freight broker needs to put the phone down sometimes. Go Vols.
